merger_name: Community Enterprise Queensland - Island & Cape Community Stores (Aurukun, Hope Vale & Badu)

targets.name: THE ARNHEM LAND PROGRESS ABORIGINAL CORPORATION

party_page.name: The Arnhem Land Progress Aboriginal Corporation

merger_description:
Community Enterprise Queensland (**CEQ**) is a Queensland Government statutory body established under the *Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Communities (Justice, Land and Other Matters) Act 1984* *(Qld)*. CEQ operates not-for-profit retail stores in remote Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities under the IBIS and ABIS brands, supplying groceries, fresh produce, household goods, hardware, café/takeaway services, and fuel.

The Arnhem Land Progress Aboriginal Corporation (**ALPA**) is an Aboriginal corporation registered with the Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission. ALPA operates community stores through its Island & Cape division across Cape York and the Torres Strait, supplying similar goods and services to CEQ’s retail stores.

CEQ proposes to acquire the operating businesses of the Aurukun Supermarket, Hope Vale Local Store, and Badu Island Community Store from ALPA (the **Acquisition**).

The Acquisition will occur via an asset purchase and includes inventory, plant and equipment, other operating assets, goodwill, and the employment of store team members. Relevant leases will be transferred or novated, subject to required approvals. The Acquisition is subject to due diligence, regulatory, and stakeholder approvals, and to the completion of transition arrangements between CEQ and ALPA.

determination_table_content.details:
Community Enterprise Queensland (CEQ) applied for a notification
waiver in respect of its proposed acquisition of the operating
businesses of the Aurukun Supermarket, Hope Vale Local Store, and
Badu Island Community Store from the Arnhem Land Progress
Aboriginal Corporation (ALPA), as described in the transaction
documents provided as part of the application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, CEQ, is a Queensland Government statutory body
established under the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander
Communities (Justice, Land and Other Matters) Act 1984 (Qld). CEQ
operates not-for-profit retail stores in remote Aboriginal and Torres
Strait Islander communities under the IBIS and ABIS brands,
supplying groceries, fresh produce, household goods, hardware,
café/takeaway services, and fuel.
The vendor, ALPA, is an Aboriginal corporation registered with the
Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission. ALPA operates
community stores through its Island & Cape division across Cape
York and the Torres Strait in each of Aurukun, Hope Vale, and Badu
Island, supplying similar goods and services to CEQ’s retail stores.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
certain publicly available information, and had regard to the factors
in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010
(Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. There is no horizontal overlap between CEQ and ALPA
in the retail supply of groceries and fuel on a local basis, as their
respective stores are in separate remote communities located
significant distances from one another.
The ACCC has also had regard to the likelihood that, if the
Acquisition were put into effect, the notification thresholds
determined under section 51ABP(1) of the Act would apply. The
ACCC considers that there is a low likelihood of the Acquisition
meeting the thresholds for notification.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
